original_test_intent: Verify a true platform-approved warm reboot preserves expected power while restarting the host, returns to the OS and restores every PCIe device without unacceptable new AER or platform error after each cycle.
original_method: After workload drain, invoke the engineering-approved warm-reset path, independently observe reset and boot milestones, and capture complete PCIe identity/link plus error/health evidence for the defined number of cycles.
manual_activity: An operator confirms workload quiescence and independently observes that the approved action follows the warm-reset boundary rather than a full DC/AC loss, then authorizes restore after per-cycle health review.
required_inputs: Platform definition of warm reboot and supported OS/BMC/reset interface
Decision whether BMC chassis power cycle meets that definition on this platform
Cycle count, reset/POST/OS timeout and service window
Power-rail or BMC telemetry that distinguishes warm reset from DC/AC interruption
Workload drain, storage flush and data-state approval
Expected PCIe BDF/device/subsystem/serial/link manifest and allowed changes
Secure command path, independent console and recovery
safety_requirements: Do not run chassis power cycle as warm until engineering confirms its platform semantics
Never expose BMC passwords or disable host verification
Confirm target SUT and workload/storage quiescence before reset
Use independent console/power evidence; uptime alone cannot classify reset type
Preserve complete error windows and device manifests without clearing logs
Stop on unexpected cold power loss, boot timeout, missing/downtrained device, AER/DPC, data/storage, thermal/power or access fault; no automatic retry
agent_execution_scope: Verify exact source and approved reset-class contract
Issue only the approved warm-reset action after confirmation and observe boot via independent console
Collect normalized per-cycle topology and health evidence
Perform no ambiguous power cycle, recovery reset, retry, workload restore or verdict
engineer_actions: Resolve authoritative warm mechanism versus chassis power cycle
Approve cycle/timing/outage, reset-class proof and recovery
Approve PCIe/error criteria and expected manifest
Review every cycle and issue PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Potentially mismatched: chassis power cycle may be a DC interruption, not a warm reboot. Fixed wait, uptime and truncated dmesg also fail the complete per-cycle Criteria and use unsafe access flags.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the platform-approved warm reset/reboot interface after the semantic decision, with state-based boot waits and complete PCIe/error evidence through secure access.

modernized_recommendation.status: PACKAGE-GATED WARM REBOOT PENDING RESET-CLASS DECISION
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Bind the approved reset interface to power-retention/console evidence, then capture reset cause, boot milestones, normalized PCIe link/device manifest and complete error window for every cycle.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds an authoritative reset class, secure execution, per-cycle topology and recovery while preserving the source conflict rather than assuming BMC semantics.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A DC or AC loss cannot substitute for warm-reset coverage; uptime only proves a reboot occurred and a log tail cannot prove full PCIe recovery.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: BMC vendors use 'power cycle' inconsistently. If standby or main rails drop, firmware and device initialization paths differ from a warm reset, so accepting that action would collapse distinct SY.2, SY.4 and SY.3 coverage.

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The Master intent and Criteria require a warm reboot, while the DeepSeek command uses BMC `chassis power cycle`, which may remove main power and behave as a DC cycle. The platform-specific reset class is not established.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The warm-reboot purpose is clear. Static review can complete while execution waits for engineering to select and classify the correct reset mechanism.

engineering_decision_pending: Resolve Functionality row 1923 Wistron-GB NV PVP HW-00005-V005: define the authoritative warm-reboot mechanism and whether BMC `chassis power cycle` preserves the required power/reset boundary or is actually a DC cycle; provide cycle/timing, reset-class evidence, full PCIe/AER criteria and recovery while keeping SY.2 distinct from SY.3/SY.4.
review_improvement: Prevents a possibly cold BMC action from masquerading as warm-reset coverage and upgrades partial uptime/log evidence to reset-class and full topology verification.
independent_technical_reasoning: Warm and cold paths exercise different firmware and endpoint initialization. A power-cycle command can cause complete PCIe fundamental reset and rail loss, while an OS warm reboot may retain portions of device power and controller state. Without independent reset-cause or rail evidence, a successful boot cannot identify which path was tested, so the method must be decided before execution rather than inferred afterward.
